sezer2009.title: Dynamic nuclear polarization of water by a nitroxide radical: rigorous treatment of the electron spin saturation and comparison with experiments at 9.2 Tesla

prandolini2009.title: High-Field Dynamic Nuclear Polarization in Aqueous Solutions
prandolini2009.location: p. 6091, paragraph following Figure 3: estimated homogeneous-line T1e*T2e from an EPR power-saturation curve; T2e from linewidth

hofer2008.title: Field Dependent Dynamic Nuclear Polarization with Radicals in Aqueous Solution
hofer2008.location: p. 3255, NMRD paragraph and effective saturation estimates; abstract gives approximate enhancement maxima
hofer2008.extraction: Numeric text transcription from indexed primary-paper text; repository abstract confirms enhancement maxima. Full PDF unavailable locally.

full_relaxation.source_location: Eqs. (37)-(38), Table 2 (45 C angular velocity), Table 5 and Appendix A1; 12 ps rotational time at approximately 40 C. Nuclear quadrupole relaxation and nonsecular hyperfine shifts were excluded in the source.
full_relaxation.calibration: No fitting to DNP or digitized saturation. Tensor anisotropy and g/A covariance construct the full relaxation operator. Spin-rotation densities are calculated from the reported angular-velocity fit; additional electron R1/R2 use the published phenomenological values. Quoted Eq. (41) line T2 values are checks, not fitted inputs for this operator.

sezer_profile.parameter_locations: Table 5; Eq. (38), Eq. (41); Fig. 5 and Fig. 6(c)

figure5.method: Red-square interior detection in the embedded JPEG; R>G+35 and R>B+25, fill holes, 4-connected components, merge fragment centers within 4 native pixels, area-weighted centers rounded to 0.01 pixel. Visually checked against the original squares; compressed/open square outlines are omitted. Reproducer: extract_marker_centers in validate_tempol_water.py. Not raw instrument data; pixels use top-left origin.

figure6c.method: Manual sparse samples of the magenta total-saturation curve in panel c, including peaks and valleys; no individual line curves used.

reduction.t2_choice: Use the published central-line T2e=25.1 ns for all three lines; the production model has a common T2e.
reduction.nitrogen_choice: No scalar nitrogen rate is inferred from the paper's full relaxation matrix. Omit this channel and quantify the reduction error.
reduction.exchange_conversion: k_ex=1/tau_H, K_ex=k_ex/C; high-temperature correlation-erasure convention of Appendix A.
reduction.hyperfine_conversion: A_iso=mean(A_tensor)*gamma_e*1e-4 Hz; the paper's g anisotropy and line-dependent shifts are omitted.
reduction.fitting: None. Published phenomenological parameters were themselves selected/estimated in the source study, so this is not a fully independent microscopic prediction.

epr_saturation_product.comparison_source: sezer2009 Eq. (40), room-temperature central 14N line; isotope and method differ
epr_saturation_product.limitations: Compare parameter compatibility only. A Bloch curve reconstructed from this product is not a set of independent saturation observations. Concentration and detailed power calibration for the cited EPR fit are not supplied here.

hofer_anchors.reported_enhancement_baseline: Unverified from available full text; these approximate maxima may use E or E-1. An offset of one remains unresolved. Closure is explicitly reported as E-1.
hofer_anchors.limitations: Saturation was inferred using DNP enhancement and NMRD, not independent ELDOR. Enhancement maxima span 5-10 mM and are approximate. NMRD reference temperature is not established as the irradiated sample temperature. No independently supplied T1e/T2e/B1 permit an unfitted population-saturation prediction. Closure is a consistency check, not independent saturation validation.
